name: Calakmul Biosphere Reserve
blurb: Maya rainforest where jaguars, tapirs and fruit trees depend on scarce water.

tip.title: Remove the jaguar
tip.text: Lower Jaguar and watch the ripple: deer, peccaries, agoutis and monkeys lose a major predator, and vultures lose a source of carrion.

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.name: Sapodilla (chicozapote)
nodes.desc: A large native tree of southern Mexico and Central America. Its sweet fruit is eaten widely and its latex is the source of chicle.

nodes.name: Gumbo-limbo
nodes.desc: A common tree of the Yucatan forest whose small fruits are recorded in the diets of many birds, bats and primates.

nodes.name: Black poisonwood
nodes.desc: A common Yucatan tree with oily fruits that birds such as toucans and parrots are recorded eating.

nodes.name: Wax mallow
nodes.desc: A leafy understory shrub with red flowers and berry-like fruit that birds feed on.

nodes.name: Geoffroy's spider monkey
nodes.desc: Fruit takes most of its feeding time, with leaves, flowers and insects as extras. Jaguars and pumas are its main adult predators.

nodes.name: Great fruit-eating bat
nodes.desc: Feeds on fruit at night, including gumbo-limbo and sapodilla, and spreads the seeds as it flies.

nodes.name: Baird's tapir
nodes.desc: Browses leaves and twigs of understory plants and eats fruit in season. Some hard seeds, such as sapodilla, pass through it intact.

nodes.name: Collared peccary
nodes.desc: A pig-like forager in herds that eats fruit, seeds, roots and some small animals. Cougars and jaguars hunt it.

nodes.name: Central American agouti
nodes.desc: Eats fruit and seeds and buries surplus seeds for later, which helps spread forest trees.

nodes.name: White-tailed deer
nodes.desc: A browser of leaves, shoots and fruit, and a main prey of jaguars in Mexico.

nodes.name: Ocellated turkey
nodes.desc: Found only on the Yucatan Peninsula. It eats insects, seeds, nuts and leaves, and roosts in trees to avoid jaguars.

nodes.name: Keel-billed toucan
nodes.desc: Eats mainly fruit, including black poisonwood and wax mallow, and also takes small animals such as birds.

nodes.name: White-nosed coati
nodes.desc: An omnivore that forages on the ground for insects, small vertebrates, eggs, carrion and fruit.

nodes.name: Gray fox
nodes.desc: An omnivorous canid that eats fruit and small mammals, and itself falls to jaguars.

nodes.name: Turkey vulture
nodes.desc: Finds and eats carrion over the forest, cleaning up the kills of the big cats.

nodes.name: Jaguar
nodes.desc: The top predator here, taking deer, peccaries, agoutis, coatis and monkeys. Calakmul and the adjoining Guatemalan forest form one of its key strongholds.

nodes.name: Puma
nodes.desc: Shares the forest and many prey with the jaguar, including deer and peccaries, and also takes monkeys.

nodes.name: Sunlight
nodes.desc: Year-round tropical light drives growth in the canopy and understory.

nodes.name: Seasonal rain
nodes.desc: Rain falls mostly in one season; the dry months test trees and animals alike.

nodes.name: Aguadas and bajos
nodes.desc: The area has little permanent surface water, so seasonal ponds and swampy low spots are vital wildlife water sources.

nodes.name: Limestone soil
nodes.desc: Thin soil over porous limestone drains quickly, which is why standing water is scarce.

nodes.name: Leaf-litter decomposers
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, fruit and carcasses, returning nutrients to thin forest soil.
